Highlights

  • Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement signed with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications, combining development and manufacturing capabilities in China with an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries.
  • Initial focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, with plans to expand into thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings and elastomers.
  • Agreement combines First Graphene's formulation and dispersion expertise with UNITEX's manufacturing and innovation capabilities, and established international supply network.
  • Provides First Graphene with a pathway into China's composites manufacturing and innovation sector and access to wider international markets, helping to accelerate the development, scale-up and global commercialisation of graphene-enhanced materials across a broad range of applications.

Sydney, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - First Graphene Limited (ASX: FGR) (FSE: M11) (OTCQB: FGPHF) ("First Graphene" or "the Company") is pleased to announce it has entered into a Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement ("the Agreement") with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. ("UNITEX"), establishing a strategic collaboration to develop and commercialise graphene enhanced carbon fibre composites and other advanced materials.

The Agreement represents a further step in First Graphene's strategy to commercialise its graphene technologies through strategic development and manufacturing partnerships. The collaboration draws on UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities in China, providing First Graphene with a pathway into China's significant composites manufacturing sector and the international markets it supplies.

Headquartered in Ningbo, China's Zhejiang province, UNITEX is a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China, the group combines material development, application engineering and industrial supply chain integration to translate material technologies into commercially viable products and solutions.

With an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries, UNITEX serves industries including automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, energy, marine, construction and sporting goods.

Its capabilities extend from customised material development and engineering support to industrial-scale manufacturing and global supply, providing a foundation for the international commercialisation of jointly developed materials.

The collaboration will combine First Graphene's expertise in graphene selection, formulation and dispersion with UNITEX's materials engineering, manufacturing infrastructure and established supply chain capabilities.

Development and commercialisation program

The initial development program will focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, building on First Graphene's internal research and development activities, which demonstrated improvements in strength and barrier properties through incorporation of graphene into carbon fibre composites.

Where the results justify further development, the parties intend to progress successful formulations through customer validation, manufacturing scale-up and commercialisation, subject to the agreement of applicable commercial terms. The Agreement term is for three years and is cancellable by either party with three months notice.

Beyond carbon fibre prepreg, the collaboration is expected to explore opportunities across thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings, elastomers and other advanced materials, broadening the potential applications and commercial reach of First Graphene's graphene technologies.

The Agreement provides First Graphene with an opportunity to leverage UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities, together with its established international customer network, to accelerate the development and industrialisation of graphene enhanced materials and bring commercially viable products to global markets.

First Graphene Managing Director and CEO, Michael Bell, said:

"Carbon fibre and advanced composites represent an increasingly important growth opportunity for First Graphene, as manufacturers seek innovative ways to improve material performance and deliver greater value to customers.

Our internal development work has demonstrated the potential of graphene to enhance the strength and barrier properties of carbon fibre composites. The next step is translating technical advances into commercially scalable products through partnerships with established manufacturers.

UNITEX brings extensive expertise in materials development, engineering and manufacturing, alongside an established international customer network. This collaboration provides FGR with a strategic pathway into China's composites manufacturing sector and expand its commercial reach across global markets.

Importantly, the opportunity extends well beyond carbon fibre. By combining our respective technical and manufacturing capabilities, we see significant potential to develop graphene-enhanced thermoplastics, coatings and other advanced materials across industrial applications.

This agreement is another important step in our strategy to move graphene innovation from development into commercial markets and expand First Graphene's international presence."

About UNITEX

UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., established in 2017 and headquartered in Ningbo, China, is part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China and the integration of China's comprehensive industrial supply chain, UNITEX brings together material development, application engineering and industrialisation to deliver customised solutions for global customers. The group serves customers in more than 100 countries, supporting a broad range of industries from material development through to commercial production and international supply.

About First Graphene Ltd (ASX: FGR)

First Graphene Limited is focused on the development of advanced materials to help industry improve. The Company is a leading supplier of graphitic materials and product formulations with a specific commercial focus on large, high-growth global markets including cement and concrete; composites and plastics; coatings, adhesives, sealants and elastomers (CASE); and energy storage applications.

One of the key outcomes these advanced materials offer is the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions, whether directly through a reduction in output of these harmful greenhouse gases or lower energy usage requirements in manufacturing, or indirectly due to enhanced performance characteristics and extending the usable life of products.

First Graphene has a robust manufacturing platform based on captive and abundant supply of high-purity raw materials, and readily scalable technologies to meet growing market demand. As well as being the world's leading supplier of its own high performance PureGRAPH® graphene product range, the Company works with multiple industry partners around the world as a supplier of graphitic materials and partner to research, develop, test and facilitate the commercial marketing of a wide range of sector-specific chemical solutions.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Battery Mineral Resources Corp. (TSXV: BMR) (OTCQB: BTRMF) ("Battery" or "BMR" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Frikkie Kruger as Chief Financial Officer of the Company, effective December 1, 2026.

Mr. Kruger, based in Massachusetts, is a Chartered Accountant (South Africa) and a member of the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants with 20 years of progressive finance leadership in the mining and resources sector, with a particular focus on copper. He has held senior finance roles in South Africa, Zambia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Middle East, South America and the United Kingdom, working with companies listed on the London, Johannesburg and Santiago stock exchanges.

Mr. Kruger was most recently Group Financial Manager at Moxico Resources PLC, which operates the Mimbula copper mine on the Zambian Copperbelt. He previously served as Chief Financial Officer of Bayete Energy Resources and as Senior Financial Reporting Manager at Enaex Africa. He has supported mining businesses through both the development and operating stages and has built finance functions from start-up. His expertise includes IFRS and U.S. GAAP reporting, multi-entity consolidation, multi-currency treasury, C1-C3 and all-in sustaining cost (AISC) modelling, payable metal calculations and SOX-aligned internal controls.

Laz Nikeas, Chief Executive of BMR, stated, "We are very pleased to welcome Frikkie to the Company. His copper-focused finance and public market experience will be a strong addition to our team."

Mr. Kruger added, "I am delighted to join Battery Mineral Resources at such an important stage for the Company and the Punitaqui Mining Complex. I look forward to working with Laz, the Board and the broader team to strengthen BMR's financial foundation, reinforce disciplined capital management and support the Company's growth strategy."

The Company also announces that it has granted 500,000 restricted share units ("RSUs") to Mr. Kruger pursuant to the Company's restricted share unit plan (the "Plan"). The RSUs will vest in three equal annual instalments commencing on the first anniversary of the date of grant and are subject to the terms and conditions of the Plan and the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

Battery Mineral Resources operates the Punitaqui Mining Complex, a historic copper, gold, and silver-producing mine in the Coquimbo region of Chile. The Company's portfolio also includes 100%-owned ESI Energy Services Inc. and North American mineral exploration assets. The Company is focused on providing shareholders with accretive exposure to copper and the global trend of electrification while targeting growth through cash flow, exploration and acquisitions in favorable mining jurisdictions. BETHESDA, Md.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Walker & Dunlop, Inc. announced today that it has arranged $270,000,000 in refinancing for The Greyson, a 28-story, 622-unit, Class A mixed-use residential tower developed by Nasser Freres in the heart of Jersey City's Journal Square neighborhood. The financing marks a significant milestone for the development, supporting its transition from construction to stabilized operations and positioning the property for long-term success.

The Greyson. Photo credits: Nasser Freres

Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory served as exclusive advisor to Nasser Freres, arranging a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan from affiliates of Apollo. The transaction was arranged by Keith Kurland, Aaron Appel, Adam Schwartz, Jonathan Schwartz, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet, and Jack Krentzman.

"Journal Square has undergone a remarkable transformation, and The Greyson exemplifies the caliber of development attracting investment to the neighborhood,” said Kurland, senior managing director of Capital Markets and co-head of Institutional Advisory at Walker & Dunlop. "With its exceptional location, extensive amenities, and proximity to Manhattan, the property is well-positioned to capitalize on the area’s continued growth. We’re pleased to have worked with Nasser Freres and Apollo to execute this transaction.”

Located at 25 Cottage Street, The Greyson encompasses 424,328 rentable square feet, including 389,328 square feet of residential and 35,000 square feet of commercial space. The property features a collection of studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences with unobstructed views of the Jersey City skyline. Designed to deliver an elevated residential experience, The Greyson offers an extensive suite of amenities, including an art gallery, children's playroom, screening room, gaming lounge, virtual reality and sports room, coffee bar, fitness center, speakeasy, and private event space. Ground-floor retail space leased to a wine bar further enhances the property’s appeal while contributing to Journal Square’s growing dining and entertainment scene.

"From the outset, our vision for The Greyson was to create something truly distinctive, a property that would help shape the next chapter of residential living in Journal Square while contributing meaningfully to the neighborhood’s continued transformation,” said Michael Sokoloff, partner at Nasser Freres. "We’ve been intentional about every aspect of this development, from its architecture and design to the amenities and experiences we’re bringing to residents. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve built and believe The Greyson will set a new standard for the neighborhood for years to come. This refinancing marks an exciting next chapter as we shift our focus to the property’s long-term success and we appreciate Walker & Dunlop’s advisory.”

Situated along the newly opened Homestead commercial corridor, the property is less than a five-minute walk from the Journal Square Transportation Center, offering direct PATH access to Lower and Midtown Manhattan in approximately 10 and 20 minutes, respectively. Journal Square has emerged as one of the New York metropolitan area's fastest-growing rental submarkets, driven by demand for transit-oriented housing and rental rates that remain comparatively affordable to those along the Jersey City Waterfront and in Manhattan.

In the first half of 2026, Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets team sourced over $13.9 billion from non-Agency capital providers, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties. This vast experience has made them a top advisor on all asset classes for many of the industry’s top developers, owners, and operators. To learn more about Walker & Dunlop’s broad financing options, visit our website.

Walker & Dunlop (NYSE: WD) is one of the largest commercial real estate finance and advisory services firms in the United States and internationally. Our ideas and capital create communities where people live, work, shop, and play. Our innovative people, breadth of our brand, and our technological capabilities make us one of the most insightful and client-focused firms in the commercial real estate industry.

Key Terms

floating-ratefinancial
A floating-rate is an interest rate on a loan, bond or other debt that moves up or down over time based on a regularly published reference number, so the payments change as market rates change. For investors, that means income and interest costs track current market conditions—like a thermostat that adjusts with room temperature—offering protection when rates rise but adding uncertainty about future cash flow.
interest-onlyfinancial
A loan or payment plan where the borrower pays only the interest for a set period while the original loan amount (the principal) stays unchanged; after that period payments typically rise to cover principal or a lump-sum principal payment is due. For investors this matters because interest-only structures change cash flows and risk: they can boost short-term income but increase the chance of payment shock or default later, similar to renting a car without paying down the purchase cost until the final bill arrives.
bridge loanfinancial
A bridge loan is a short-term loan used to quickly provide funds until a larger, long-term financing option is in place. It acts like a temporary bridge, helping individuals or businesses cover immediate expenses or complete transactions without delay. For investors, it’s important because it offers quick access to cash but often comes with higher costs and short repayment periods.

The proposed transaction was opportunistic to refinance the Company’s existing 4.625% senior notes well in advance of their May 2028 maturity. Everforth’s strong free cash flow and liquidity position provide the Company with significant financial flexibility. Everforth remains committed to using its free cash flow to reduce debt and further strengthen the balance sheet. senior notesfinancial
Senior notes are a type of loan that a company borrows from investors, promising to pay it back with interest. This makes senior notes safer for investors compared to other types of loans or bonds.
aggregate principal amountfinancial
The aggregate principal amount is the total amount of money borrowed through a bond or loan that the borrower promises to repay. It’s like the original price tag on a loan or bond, showing how much money is involved in the deal. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Plurilock Security Inc. (TSXV: PLUR) (OTCQB: PLCKF) ("Plurilock" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that, at the special meeting (the "Meeting") of holders (the "Shareholders") of common shares of Plurilock (each, a "Plurilock Share" and, collectively, the "Plurilock Shares") held on November 18, 2026, Shareholders voted in favour of the special resolution (the "Arrangement Resolution") approving the previously announced plan of arrangement (the "Arrangement") with Quantum eMotion Corp. ("QeM"). The Arrangement is being completed pursuant to the terms and conditions of a definitive arrangement agreement between Plurilock and QeM dated September 28, 2026 (the "Arrangement Agreement").

Under the Arrangement, QeM will acquire all of the issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares. Shareholders will receive C$0.084 in cash and 0.0763 of a common share of QeM (each whole common share of QeM, a "QeM Share") in exchange for each Plurilock Share they hold (together, the "Consideration"), implying total consideration of C$0.28 per Plurilock Share. Further, all outstanding options to acquire Plurilock Shares ("Plurilock Options") will be cancelled in exchange for QeM Shares and cash in the same proportions as the Consideration having a value equal to the amount (if any) by which C$0.28 exceeds the applicable exercise price per Plurilock Option. All outstanding restricted share units will vest immediately prior to the effective time of the Arrangement and be settled for the Consideration. All outstanding warrants and convertible debentures of Plurilock will, in accordance with their terms and without further action by the holders thereof, entitle the holders to receive, upon exercise or conversion, the Consideration in lieu of Plurilock Shares.

Shareholders holding a total of 68,226,137 Plurilock Shares were represented in person or by proxy at the Meeting, representing 60.38% of the 112,989,001 issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares entitled to vote as of October 1, 2026, the record date for the Meeting.

The Arrangement required the approval of: (i) at least two-thirds (66⅔%) of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting; and (ii) a majority of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting, excluding Plurilock Shares held by "interested parties" as defined in Multilateral Instrument 61-101 - Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101").

At the Meeting, 99.58% of the votes cast by Shareholders (99.54% after excluding Plurilock Shares required to be excluded under MI 61-101) were in favour of the Arrangement Resolution.

The Company will seek a final order (the "Final Order") of the Supreme Court of British Columbia (the "Court") to approve the Arrangement on November 20, 2026. Completion of the Arrangement is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions for a transaction of this nature, including receipt of the Final Order. Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the closing conditions, it is expected that the Arrangement will be completed shortly after the receipt of the Final Order. Following completion of the Arrangement, it is expected that the Plurilock Shares will be delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV").

About Quantum eMotion Corp.

Quantum eMotion Corp. (NYSE American: QNC) (TSXV: QNC) (FSE: 34Q0) is developing quantum-secure cybersecurity technologies designed to protect digital systems, communications and data in an increasingly complex cyber-threat environment. QeM's technology portfolio combines quantum-generated entropy, quantum-safe cryptography and cybersecurity technologies designed for applications across enterprise, cloud, communications, critical infrastructure and other security-sensitive environments. For more information, visit www.quantumemotion.com.

About Plurilock Security Inc.

Plurilock sells cybersecurity solutions and delivers critical IT and cybersecurity services to public- and private-sector organizations. Through its operating businesses and predecessor operations, Plurilock has a 25-plus-year operating history, serves hundreds of customers and maintains procurement and contract channels in Canada, the United States and NATO. Its capabilities include Critical Services, cybersecurity and IT modernization, managed services, data protection, cloud security, identity and access management, and AI-enabled security technologies. SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE), a global leader in power solutions, today announced that it has been named to TIME's list of America's Top Manufacturers of 2027.

America's Top Manufacturers of 2027

The list, developed by TIME and Statista, recognizes 250 U.S. manufacturers based on financial performance, innovation capacity and employment metrics. Companies were evaluated using measures including revenue growth, research and development investment, workforce growth and retention, and workplace safety.

“At Bloom, technology and manufacturing innovation go hand in hand,” said Satish Chitoori, Chief Operations Officer at Bloom Energy. “We have spent years building the people, processes and manufacturing capability required to take a highly complex energy technology and produce it at scale in the United States. That capability matters more than ever as demand for power is growing at a pace the traditional infrastructure model was not designed to meet. The digital era requires digital power solutions, and Bloom meets that need for a wide range of essential industries. This recognition belongs to the teams who make that possible every day.”

Bloom manufactures its fuel cell technology in the United States, with manufacturing operations in Fremont, California, and Newark, Delaware. The company’s platform provides clean, highly reliable power that can be rapidly deployed onsite, helping customers meet growing electricity requirements as power demand accelerates across data centers, commercial and industrial sectors, and other critical industries.

TIME's recognition comes as U.S. manufacturing is increasingly important to the infrastructure required to support AI and data center growth. In announcing the 2027 list, TIME highlighted electrical equipment as the sector with the largest representation among America's top manufacturers and pointed to surging demand associated with data center construction.

TIME and Statista considered thousands of companies with at least $100 million in 2025 revenue and U.S. production facilities. The analysis drew on company disclosures, public databases, patent analytics, Form 10-K filings, ESG and CSR reports, and Occupational Safety and Health Administration data.

The full TIME list and methodology are available here.

About Bloom Energy

Bloom Energy empowers enterprises to meet soaring energy demands and responsibly take charge of their power needs. The company’s fuel cell systems provide ultra-reliable, clean and highly scalable onsite electricity for Fortune 500 customers around the world, including data centers, semiconductor manufacturing, large utilities and other commercial and industrial sectors, as well as mission-critical organizations in local communities, such as hospitals, college campuses and retailers. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, Bloom Energy employs more than 2,000 people worldwide and manufactures its systems in the United States. For more information, visit BloomEnergy.com.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Copper Lake Resources Ltd. (TSXV: CPL) (FSE: W0I0) ("Copper Lake" or the "Company") announces that its Board of Directors has granted an aggregate of 4,100,000 incentive stock options (the "Options") to directors, officers and consultants of the Company pursuant to the Company's stock option plan.

Each Option entitles the holder to purchase one common share of the Company at an exercise price of $0.25 per share until November 18, 2031. The Options vested immediately upon grant. Of the Options granted, 1,650,000 were granted to directors and officers of the Company and 2,450,000 were granted to consultants of the Company.

The Options, and any common shares issued upon the exercise of the Options prior to March 19, 2027, are subject to a four-month hold period in accordance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange. The grant of the Options is subject to the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

ABOUT COPPER LAKE RESOURCES

Copper Lake Resources Ltd. is a publicly traded Canadian mineral exploration and development company with interests in two projects both located in Ontario.

The Marshall Lake high-grade VMS copper, zinc, silver and gold project, comprises an area of approximately 220 square km located 120 km north of Geraldton, Ontario and is just 22 km north of the main CNR rail line. Copper Lake has an 82.97% interest in the joint ventured property, which consists of 233 claims and 52 mining leases. The project also includes 148 claim cells staked in 2018 and 2020 that are 100% owned and not subject to any royalties. These newer claims add approximately 30 square km to the property.

In addition to the original Marshall Lake property above, Marshall Lake also includes the Sollas Lake and Summit Lake properties, which are 100% owned by the Company and are not subject to any royalties. The Sollas Lake property consists of 20 claim cells comprising an area of 4 square km on the east side of the Marshall Lake property where historical EM airborne geophysical surveys have outlined strong conductors on the property hosted within the same favorable felsic volcanic units. The Summit Lake property currently consists of 100 claim cells comprising an area of 20.5 square km, is accessible year-round, and is located immediately west of the original Marshall Lake property. The Marshall Lake project is located in the traditional territories of Aroland and Animbiigoo Zaagi'igan Anishinaabek ("AZA") First Nations.

Copper Lake has a 69.79% joint venture interest in the Norton Lake nickel, copper, cobalt, and palladium PGM property, located in the southern Ring of Fire area, is approximately 100 km north of the Marshall Lake Property. The Company filed an updated NI 43-101 in October 2023 with a mineral resource of open pit and underground Measured + Indicated Resources of 1,795,000 tonnes at an average grade of 0.72% NI, 0.69% Cu, 339 ppm Co, 0.52 g/t Pd, 0.17 g/t Pt and containing 28.3Mlbs of nickel and 27.3Mlbs of copper. The Norton Lake property is located in the traditional territories of Eabametoong ("Fort Hope") and Neskantaga First Nations.

  • Poster presented today at CTOS 2026 expands on the survival data first reported in the abstract (announced 11 November 2026), which showed a 12-month disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% in patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma.
  • Patients with post-treatment tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels.
  • Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels.
  • Results build on previously reported strong pathological responses and further support the potential of efti-based combination therapy.

SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Immutep Limited (ASX: IMM; NASDAQ: IMMP) (“Immutep” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel LAG-3 immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune diseases, today announced new data from the investigator-initiated EFTISARC-NEO Phase II study presented at the Connective Tissue Oncology Society (CTOS) 2026 Annual Meeting (Poster number P 448).

The study is evaluating Immutep’s eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy before surgery in patients with high-risk, resectable soft tissue sarcoma. Forty patients were enrolled, and 38 patients underwent surgery and were included in the survival evaluation.

The latest analysis currently shows a disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% at 12 months. The current Kaplan-Meier estimate at 18 months is also 81.1%, although this later time point remains immature, and follow-up is ongoing. Among the 38 patients who underwent surgery and were evaluated, eight patients had experienced disease recurrence at the data cut-off (April 30, 2026).

Table 1 – Survival results for soft tissue sarcoma patients from EFTISARC-NEO

OutcomeLatest Analysis
12-month disease-free survival (mature)81.1%
18-month disease-free survival (immature)81.1%
12-month local recurrence-free survival94.1%
12-month distant metastasis-free survival86.2%
Median follow-up19.1 months


In addition, exploratory analyses showed that higher levels of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and greater hyalinisation and fibrosis after treatment may be associated with better DFS. In particular, patients with post-treatment TIL levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels. Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels of hyalinisation and fibrosis. The presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and baseline expression of PD-L1, LAG-3 and TIGIT did not correlate with survival outcomes.

These survival and exploratory findings build on previously reported EFTISARC-NEO results in which the trial met its primary endpoint with a median tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis of 51.5% following neoadjuvant therapy with efti, pembrolizumab and radiotherapy. The new data are consistent with efti's mechanism of action, in which activation of antigen-presenting cells drives a stronger anti-tumour T cell response, and suggest that a stronger immune response in the tumour may be associated with improved patient survival outcomes.

Pawel Sobczuk, MD PhD, one of the Principal Investigators of EFTISARC-NEO, said: “These results are highly encouraging for patients with high-risk soft tissue sarcoma, where recurrence remains a major concern despite surgery and radiotherapy. Disease-free survival of approximately 81% maintained through 12 months and on a preliminary basis also at 18 months is an important observation, and the association between a strong immune response in the tumour and better disease-free survival is particularly compelling. Together with the substantial pathological responses previously reported, the findings reinforce the potential of this novel neoadjuvant approach and provide a strong rationale for continued follow-up and further clinical evaluation.”

Marc Voigt, CEO of Immutep, said: “With the data to date, EFTISARC-NEO is delivering an increasingly coherent and encouraging picture. The marked difference in outcomes between patients with higher and lower post-treatment immune cell infiltration is especially notable and is consistent with efti’s potential to help generate a stronger anti-tumour immune response. We believe these results strengthen the rationale for further potential clinical development in this indication, where patients remain in need of more effective treatment options.”

The poster is available on the Posters & Publications page of Immutep’s website.

Next Steps

Immutep anticipates reporting additional data from EFTISARC-NEO in CY2027.

Subject to regulatory interactions, manufacturing timelines, partnering arrangements and available resources, the Company is preparing to advance efti into a registration-directed clinical trial in neoadjuvant soft tissue sarcoma, targeting initiation in H2 CY2027.

About EFTISARC-NEO

EFTISARC-NEO is an investigator-initiated, open-label Phase II trial evaluating eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment for patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma. The trial is led by the Maria Skłodowska-Curie National Research Institute of Oncology in Warsaw, Poland, and is primarily funded by a grant from the Polish Medical Research Agency, with Immutep supplying efti.

The primary endpoint is pathological response, measured as the percentage of tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis at resection. Secondary endpoints include safety, disease-free survival, local recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, radiological response and health-related quality of life. Forty patients were enrolled, with enrolment completed in January 2025 (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06128863).

About Eftilagimod Alfa (efti)

Eftilagimod alfa (efti) is Immutep’s proprietary soluble LAG-3 protein and MHC Class II agonist that activates antigen-presenting cells through the MHC Class II pathway, engaging both innate and adaptive immunity, including the priming of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and the production of co-stimulatory signals and cytokines. Its favourable safety profile enables combination with anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy. Efti has received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and first-line non-small cell lung cancer, and Orphan Drug Designation in soft tissue sarcoma.

About Immutep

Immutep is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. The Company is a pioneer in the understanding and advancement of therapeutics related to Lymphocyte Activation Gene-3 (LAG-3), and its diversified product portfolio harnesses LAG-3’s ability to stimulate or suppress the immune response. Immutep is dedicated to leveraging its expertise to bring innovative treatment options to patients in need and to maximise value for shareholders. For more information, please visit www.immutep.com.

Approval based on Phase 3 NIMBLE results demonstrating rapid, deep and sustained disease control that is maintained throughout three-month dosing intervals

Livsayis is Regeneron's first approved siRNA therapy and neurology medicine

TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Livsayis™ (cemdisiran) for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody-positive, the predominant form of the disease. Livsayis is a novel, complement component factor 5 (C5)-directed small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic that reduces levels of circulating C5 protein, limiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of the disease. It is the first and only approved siRNA therapy in gMG and the only FDA-approved gMG treatment administered subcutaneously four times a year.

“For people living with gMG, every day can be unpredictable, due to fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigue. They may also experience severe exacerbations that can be life-threatening. Many still experience suboptimal disease control, whether from waning of therapeutic effect, inadequate response or high treatment burden,” said Tuan Vu, M.D., Professor of Neurology at the University of South Florida Morsani College of Medicine, Division Director for Neuromuscular Medicine and EMG Laboratories, and a global principal investigator of the NIMBLE trial. “In the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial, Livsayis delivered rapid, deep disease control – maintained through the end of dosing intervals – and offers a four-times-a-year subcutaneous dosing schedule. These results highlight how a first-of-its-kind approach can address a key driver of disease and provide a compelling treatment option.”

The FDA approval was based on results from the Phase 3 NIMBLE trial. Livsayis demonstrated the following least square mean change from baseline:

  • 4.5-point improvement on the Myasthenia Gravis-Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) total score at 24 weeks (0.4 standard error [SE]) compared to a 2.2-point improvement with placebo (0.5 SE). This corresponded to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.3 points (p=0.0005). MG-ADL is a clinician-administered patient-reported assessment of daily functions impacted by gMG, such as talking, chewing, swallowing, breathing, vision and mobility. The proportion of MG-ADL responders with at least 3-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (76.6%) compared to placebo (44.1%, p<0.001).
  • 4.2-point improvement in Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) total score at 24 weeks (0.6 SE) compared to a 1.5-point improvement with placebo (0.7 SE), corresponding to a placebo-adjusted improvement of 2.8 points (p=0.0015). QMG is a clinician-administered assessment of muscle function, including vision, speaking/swallowing, breathing and limb mobility. The proportion of QMG responders with at least a 5-point improvement at week 24 was greater for Livsayis (48.4%) compared to placebo (19.0%, p<0.001).
  • Rapid onset of clinically meaningful benefit in MG-ADL (2.5 points), with improvements seen as early as two weeks of starting treatment that deepened over time.
  • Sustained disease control and symptom relief through 24 weeks, with MG-ADL scores maintained and no indication of waning efficacy.

The prescribing information for Livsayis includes a Boxed Warning for serious meningococcal infections in addition to warnings and precautions for other serious infections, consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. The most common adverse reactions (≥5%) in patients treated with Livsayis and more frequently than placebo were injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections. Livsayis is available only through a restricted program called the Livsayis Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS), which is also consistent with other FDA-approved medicines that reduce C5 activity. Details of the Important Safety Information are included below.

“Livsayis is Regeneron’s first approved medicine in neurology, and an important new option for people living with generalized myasthenia gravis who need effective disease control without a heavy treatment burden,” said George D. Yancopoulos, M.D., Ph.D., Board Co-Chair, President and Chief Scientific Officer of Regeneron. “As Regeneron’s first approved siRNA therapy, this approval marks a meaningful step forward for our neuroscience pipeline as we relentlessly pursue bold, new approaches to transform care for people living with serious neurological diseases.”

“Individuals living with gMG experience profound muscle weakness that can affect how they talk, see, breathe and move, and with it their ability to carry out everyday activities,” said Samantha Masterson, President & CEO, Myasthenia Gravis Foundation of America. “This approval is a positive milestone for the gMG community, reflecting continued progress on outcomes that matter most to patients. With Livsayis, those living with generalized myasthenia gravis have a new option that may help maintain disease control while reducing the burden treatment can place on daily life.”

Regeneron is committed to supporting people living with rare diseases and ensuring patients who have been prescribed Livsayis access to their medication. Regeneron’s myRARE™ program offers resources to help patients and healthcare providers, including product information, insurance benefit verification, and information about potential financial support. To learn about myRARE, visit myRARE.com or call 1-833-4my-RARE (1-833-469-7273).

A regulatory submission for Livsayis for the treatment of gMG is currently under review in the European Union, with a decision anticipated in the second half of 2027. Regulatory submissions are planned in additional markets, including Japan.

About gMG
gMG is a rare, chronic autoimmune disease characterized by unpredictable, debilitating and potentially life-threatening muscle weakness. In the most common form of the disease, abnormal anti-AChR antibodies activate the complement system including C5, disrupting communication between nerves and muscles, which contributes to damage at the neuromuscular junction. For these patients, the disease affects muscles throughout the body, resulting in extreme fatigue and difficulties with facial expression, speech, swallowing, mobility, breathing as well as severe exacerbations, including myasthenic crisis that can impair breathing to the point of requiring hospitalization. Worldwide, an estimated 150 to 200 out of every million people have MG. In the U.S., the disease impacts approximately 85,000 people.

About Livsayis
Livsayis is the first approved siRNA therapy for gMG and the only gMG treatment FDA-approved to be administered subcutaneously four times per year (every three months).

Livsayis is a complement C5-directed siRNA that degrades the messenger RNA (mRNA) that encodes the C5 protein, thereby blocking C5 production, reducing circulating levels of C5 and inhibiting terminal complement activation, a key driver of AChR-positive gMG.

Regeneron is solely responsible for the development, manufacturing, and commercialization of Livsayis through a worldwide licensing agreement with Alnylam.

About the NIMBLE trial
NIMBLE is the largest global, interventional gMG trial conducted to date. In this ongoing Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, Livsayis is being evaluated in patients with anti-AChR antibody-positive gMG who can continue background immunosuppressants based on the investigator’s discretion. Participants were randomized to receive one of four subcutaneous regimens: Livsayis every three months; a combination of Livsayis and a C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; C5-inhibiting monoclonal antibody every 4 weeks; or placebo every 4 weeks.

The primary endpoint assessed changes in the MG-ADL total score from baseline to week 24. The MG-ADL scale is an eight-question clinician-administered, patient-reported tool that measures how gMG affects aspects of daily life and provides a total score ranging from 0 to 24. The key secondary endpoint was the change from baseline in QMG total score at week 24. The QMG is a clinician-administered 13-item standardized assessment evaluating muscle function that provides a total score ranging from 0 to 39. In both MG-ADL and QMG, a higher total score indicates greater disease severity, and a larger reduction in total score indicates greater improvement in disease symptoms and better treatment effect.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about LIVSAYIS?

LIVSAYIS is a medicine that affects part of your immune system. LIVSAYIS may lower the ability of your immune system to fight certain infections.

  • LIVSAYIS increases your chance of getting serious meningococcal infections caused by Neisseria meningitidis bacteria. Meningococcal infections may quickly become life-threatening or cause death if not recognized and treated early.
    • You must complete your meningococcal vaccines at least 2 weeks before your first dose of LIVSAYIS.
    • If you have not completed your meningococcal vaccines, and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you should receive the required vaccines as soon as possible.
    • If you have not been vaccinated and LIVSAYIS must be started right away, you must also receive antibiotics.
    • If you had a meningococcal vaccine in the past, you might need additional vaccination before starting LIVSAYIS. Your healthcare provider will decide if you need additional meningococcal vaccination.
    • Meningococcal vaccines do not prevent all meningococcal infections. Call your healthcare provider or get emergency medical help right away if you get any of these signs and symptoms of a meningococcal infection: fever, fever and a rash, fever with high heart rate, headache with nausea or vomiting, headache and a fever, headache with a stiff neck or stiff back, confusion, muscle aches with flu-like symptoms, or eyes sensitive to light

Your healthcare provider will give you a Patient Safety Card about the risk of serious meningococcal infection. Carry it with you at all times during treatment and for 12 months after your last LIVSAYIS dose. Your risk of meningococcal infection may continue for several months after your last dose of LIVSAYIS. It is important to show this card to any healthcare provider who treats you. This will help them diagnose and treat you quickly.

LIVSAYIS is only available through a program called the LIVSAYIS Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). Before you can receive LIVSAYIS, your healthcare provider must: enroll in the LIVSAYIS REMS program; counsel you about the risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you the Patient Guide that explains your risk of serious meningococcal infections; give you a Patient Safety Card that has important information about the signs and symptoms of meningococcal infections; make sure that you are vaccinated against serious infections caused by meningococcal bacteria, and that you receive antibiotics if you need to start LIVSAYIS right away and you are not up-to-date on your vaccines.

LIVSAYIS may also increase the risk of other types of serious infections especially those caused by encapsulated bacteria, including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Certain people may be at risk of serious infections with gonorrhea. Talk to your healthcare provider about whether you are at risk for gonorrhea infection, about gonorrhea prevention, and regular testing.

Call your healthcare provider right away if you have new signs or symptoms of infection.

Who should not receive LIVSAYIS?

  • Do not receive LIVSAYIS if you have a serious meningococcal infection when you are starting LIVSAYIS treatment.

Before you receive LIVSAYIS, tell your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions, including if you:

  • Have an infection or fever
  • Are pregnant or plan to be pregnant. It is not known whether LIVSAYIS will harm your unborn baby
  • Are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if LIVSAYIS passes into your breast milk

Tell your healthcare provider about medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Know the medicines you take and the vaccines you receive. Keep a list of them to show your healthcare provider and pharmacist when you get a new medicine.

The most common side effects in people with gMG treated with LIVSAYIS include: injection site reactions, viral infections and urinary tract infections.
Tell your healthcare provider about any side effect that bothers you or that does not go away. These are not all the possible side effects of LIVSAYIS. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Please see full Prescribing Information, including Boxed WARNING, and Medication Guide for LIVSAYIS.

What is LIVSAYIS?
LIVSAYIS is a prescription medicine used to treat a disease called generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adults who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive.

It is not known if LIVSAYIS is safe and effective in children.

— A novel EGFR-directed ATTC with a potent pan-KRAS payload designed to overcome resistance and systemic toxicity associated with EGFR/KRAS inhibition —

— Broad-spectrum activity across multiple KRAS mutations, combining inhibition of both ON and OFF states to intercept adaptive resistance —

HONG KONG and SHANGHAI and FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HUTCHMED (China) Limited (“HUTCHMED” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq/AIM:​HCM; HKEX:​13) today announces preclinical data for HMPL-A830 presented at the EORTC-NCI-AACR International Conference on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics, held on November 18–20, 2026, in Barcelona, Spain. HMPL-A830 is a first-in-class Antibody-Targeted Therapy Conjugate (“ATTC”) drug candidate comprises a highly selective and potent KRAS small molecule inhibitor payload conjugated to an anti‑epidermal growth factor receptor (“EGFR”) antibody.

RAS mutations represent one of the most prevalent and well-established drivers in human oncology, driving the progression and aggressive pathology of multiple solid tumors. While recent targeted therapies have validated KRAS (the most dominant RAS isoform) as a viable therapeutic target, significant clinical gaps remain, including safety limitations and disease progression driven by acquired resistance, often mediated by upstream receptor tyrosine kinase upregulation. HMPL-A830 is designed to address this unmet need by delivering a KRAS inhibitor directly to EGFR-expressing tumors, while simultaneously blocking EGFR and KRAS signaling to enhance efficacy, durability, and tolerability.

In vitro profiling demonstrated that its pan-KRAS payload exhibits a dual-action mechanism, simultaneously blocking both KRAS “ON” (GTP-RAF1 binding) and “OFF” (GDP-to-GTP exchange) activities. Potent antiproliferative activity was observed across a broad panel of 55 tumor cell lines harboring diverse KRAS alterations, including G12C, G12D, G12V and G13D mutations, as well as wild-type amplification. HMPL-A830 exhibited high binding affinity and rapid internalization into EGFR-positive cells. It also demonstrated a strong bystander killing effect, effectively eliminating neighboring EGFR-negative tumor cells, while maintaining robust antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity.

In mouse models, HMPL-A830 showed dose-dependent and robust antitumor efficacy across various EGFR-positive tumor models harboring KRAS alterations. HMPL-A830 achieved more durable tumor regressions than KRAS G12C inhibitors and outperformed several comparative regimens, including its unconjugated antibody, a pan-RAS inhibitor (administered alone or in combination with cetuximab), and a TROP2-targeted Topo I-inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) analyses confirmed a stronger and more sustained inhibition of EGFR/KRAS downstream signaling than the naked antibody, alongside a stable drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR) maintained in mouse, monkey, and human plasma.

In September 2026, HUTCHMED Limited (a subsidiary of the Company) entered into an exclusive development and license agreement with a subsidiary of GSK plc (“GSK”), granting the GSK subsidiary worldwide rights excluding Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan to develop and commercialize HMPL-A830. HUTCHMED Limited is responsible for the global Phase I development program of HMPL-A830. The GSK subsidiary will be responsible for all subsequent clinical development and commercialization activities outside of Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. 

The Phase Ia part of an ongoing global Phase I trial is currently evaluating HMPL-A830 in patients with unresectable, advanced, or metastatic solid tumors (NCT07718581).

About HUTCHMED ATTCs

HUTCHMED’s ATTCs represent a next-generation approach to precision oncology, combining monoclonal antibodies with proprietary small-molecule inhibitor payload platforms to deliver dual mechanisms of action. Unlike traditional cytotoxin-based antibody-drug conjugates, ATTCs combine targeted therapies to achieve synergistic anti-tumor activity and durable responses in preclinical models, outperforming standalone antibody or small-molecule inhibitor components in both efficacy and safety.

Built on over 20 years of targeted therapy expertise, the ATTC platforms enable development of drug candidates across diverse cancer types. By leveraging antibody-guided delivery and tumor-specific payload release, ATTCs improve accessibility to tumors and reduce off-tumor toxicity. This may overcome the on-target, off-tumor toxicity limitations of systemically-delivered small molecule inhibitors, which in turn could ensure safer long-term use and support combinations with chemotherapy and immunotherapy in earlier-line treatments.

About KRAS

RAS mutations represent one of the most prevalent and well-established drivers in human oncology, driving the progression and aggressive pathology of multiple solid tumors. KRAS, the most dominant RAS isoform, is mutated in approximately 44% of colorectal cancer (“CRC”), 34% of lung adenocarcinoma and up to 89% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (“PDAC”) patients.1 KRAS regulates key downstream pathways, including RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR, to drive cell differentiation, proliferation, and survival.

While recent targeted therapies have validated KRAS as a viable therapeutic target, significant clinical gaps persist, particularly for patients with non-G12C mutations. Most patients eventually experience disease progression driven by acquired resistance, largely fueled by upstream receptor tyrosine kinase upregulation and secondary KRAS alterations. Beyond mutation coverage, systemic delivery of pan-KRAS and pan-RAS inhibitors is associated with on-target toxicities, such as dermatological toxicity reflecting RAS pathway inhibition in normal tissue. These present challenges for dosing, long-term tolerability, and combination with cytotoxic chemotherapy or immunotherapy backbones that constitute frontline standard-of-care.

About EGFR

EGFR is a widely expressed receptor tyrosine kinase and established driver of tumor cell proliferation, survival, and disease progression across multiple solid tumors, including CRC, PDAC, and non-small cell lung cancer (“NSCLC”). Signaling through EGFR activates the downstream RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathways, positioning the receptor immediately upstream of KRAS. EGFR has also emerged as a key mediator of resistance to KRAS-targeted therapies, particularly in CRC, where adaptive feedback and increased upstream EGFR signaling reactivate the MAPK pathway and limit the depth and durability of KRAS inhibition. Together, these provide a strong rationale for the dual targeting of EGFR and KRAS, not only in CRC but also additional indications such as PDAC and NSCLC.

About HUTCHMED

HUTCHMED (Nasdaq/AIM: HCM; HKEX: 13) is an innovative, commercial-stage, biopharmaceutical company. It is committed to the discovery and global development and commercialization of targeted therapies and immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer and immunological diseases. Since inception it has focused on bringing drug candidates from in-house discovery to patients around the world, with its first four medicines marketed in China, the first of which is also approved around the world including in the US, Europe and Japan. SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- JOYY Inc. (NASDAQ: JOYY) (“JOYY” or the “Company”), a global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter of 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights1

  • Net revenues were US$624.6 million, an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    • Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million, compared with US$19.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$13.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP EBITDA2 was US$55.7 million, an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and compared with US$56.9 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest of JOYY3 was US$59.6 million, compared with US$62.0 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$51.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Non-GAAP net income from continuing operations attributable to controlling interest and common shareholders of JOYY4 was US$67.1 million, compared with US$72.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$63.5 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Net Cash5 as of September 30, 2026 was US$2,940.5 million.
  • Net Cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million, compared with US$73.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Global community:

  • Global average mobile MAUs6 reached 278.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, up by 4.7% from 266.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and up by 0.6% from 277.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. The Company continued to optimize its marketing strategies to focus on return on investment (ROI) and high-value users.

Social Entertainment:

  • In the third quarter, Social Entertainment revenues increased by 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, with live streaming revenues reaching US$419.8 million, an 8.1% increase from the corresponding period of 2025. By region, live streaming revenues showed year-over-year growth across all four geographical areas.
  • In the third quarter, core live streaming paying users7 increased by 8.1% year over year to 1.64 million, while ARPPU8 was US$218.7.
  • Bigo Live continued to make enhancements across content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. In content operations, the Company refined its cross-regional content algorithms, expanded live translation coverage and noise-resilient speech recognition, enabling users to discover diverse content and interact with streamers across regions. Improved onboarding and guidance for newly signed streamers contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point sequential increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream. The Company also continued to expand AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts. In September 2026, AI-generated interactive virtual gifts accounted for 35.4% of total virtual gift consumption on Bigo Live.

B2B Initiatives: Advertising Technology and Smart Commerce

  • Beginning in 2022, the Company ramped up efforts to diversify its revenue streams, cultivating its new initiatives in advertising technology and smart commerce. The Company has made steady progress advancing towards its strategic positioning as a global tech company powered by multiple growth engines. In the third quarter, total non-live streaming revenues reached US$204.7 million, up by 34.9% year over year, representing 32.8% of total net revenues of the Company, compared with 28.1% in the corresponding period of 2025.

BIGO Ads:

  • BIGO Ads is a global AI-powered programmatic advertising platform. Launched to provide one-stop marketing and monetization solutions, it leverages deep learning, real-time bidding, and smart bidding models to enable brands to scale user acquisition and app developers to effectively unlock monetization potential through connecting premium global demand.
  • In the third quarter, BIGO Ads’ total revenues grew by 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million. In particular, BIGO Audience Network, which includes third-party advertising revenues generated on network partners’ traffic properties, maintained robust growth, with revenues increasing by 52.3% year over year.
  • BIGO Ads has access to a vast traffic pool, comprising the Company’s own global average mobile MAU base and an extensive network of third-party traffic through seamless integration of developer traffic across major channels. During the third quarter, Software Development Kit (SDK) traffic scale continued to expand, increasing by 55.6% year over year.
  • Broader traffic coverage, multi-vertical advertiser expansion, and ongoing algorithm optimization continued to fuel growth. Web-based demand grew approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, alongside solid performance from in-app demand.
  • BIGO Ads continued to invest in its algorithm and engineering infrastructure during the quarter. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, BIGO Ads broadened its data inputs for model training, improving predictions of conversion probability and user lifetime value. The platform also upgraded its model architecture to support different conversion objectives and traffic types, while refining its bidding algorithm to better assess the value of each ad impression and allocate advertiser budgets more effectively.

Shopline:

  • Shopline serves as a global AI-powered operating system for modern retail. Beyond storefront creation, Shopline offers a deeply integrated suite of merchant services across payments, logistics, marketing, and data analytics. It is an open, extensible omnichannel platform that enables merchants to manage the full commerce value chain from store setup and transactions to fulfillment, customer acquisition, and lifecycle engagement. Shopline has helped merchants in diverse industries across multiple markets to launch and scale their businesses.
  • Shopline currently generates revenues from recurring software subscription fees and a suite of transaction-based value-added services, including localized payment processing (Shopline Payments) and marketing solutions.
  • In the third quarter, Shopline generated revenues of US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter. Notably, cross-border merchants revenue increased by 77.8% year over year. The Company continued to enhance Shopline Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management, helping merchants manage cross-border payments more easily and efficiently.
  • As AI platforms and agents emerge as new channels for product discovery and purchasing, Shopline continued to strengthen its AI Commerce capabilities. On the ecosystem front, Shopline expanded its integrations with leading AI platforms and AI agents, and enhanced its AI tools and interfaces for developers. On the merchant operations front, the Company rolled out its AI-powered commerce assistant, Shopline Omi, spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, multilingual support, and detailed store performance analysis.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY, commented, “This quarter, we made further progress toward becoming a global technology company powered by multiple growth engines. Total net revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Our Social Entertainment business remained on a steady course, while BIGO Ads and Shopline sustained robust performances, driving solid topline expansion and strong operating cash flow generation. We remain steadfast in our commitment to shareholder returns, having returned a total of US$536.0 million year-to-date through November 13, 2026, comprising US$216.2 million in dividends and US$319.8 million in share repurchases.

Social Entertainment revenues grew 8.8% year over year to US$441.0 million, supported by continued enhancements to Bigo Live’s content operations, streamer ecosystem, and AI-driven capabilities. Live streaming revenues and core live streaming paying users both increased 8.1% year over year. BIGO Ads revenues rose 39.6% year over year to US$145.7 million, led by 52.3% year-over-year growth in BIGO Audience Network as we expanded our traffic network, diversified advertiser demand, and improved our algorithms and ad delivery. Shopline revenues reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year, supported by continued expansion among cross-border merchants and strong momentum in Shopline Payments. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

NET REVENUES

Net revenues were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment net revenues increased by 8.8% to US$441.0 million from US$405.5 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by higher live streaming revenues, as expanded content categories and enhanced localized operations contributed to stronger user engagement and paying conversion across key markets.

BIGO Ads net revenues increased by 39.6% to US$145.7 million from US$104.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by expansion of traffic, elevated advertiser demand across regions and verticals, and enhanced algorithm performance that resulted in improved advertisement delivery efficiency and higher advertiser spending.

Shopline net revenues increased by 24.7% to US$37.8 million from US$30.3 million in the corresponding period of 2025, and by 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily driven by continued merchant adoption and deeper penetration of value-added services.

COST OF REVENUES AND GROSS PROFIT

Cost of revenues was US$407.4 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$347.1 million in the corresponding period of 2025 and US$389.2 million in the second quarter of 2026.

Social Entertainment’s cost of revenues increased by 7.4% year over year to US$274.3 million, and by 3.7% from US$264.6 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher revenue-sharing fees and content costs of US$28.4 million and US$7.9 million, respectively.

BIGO Ads’ cost of revenues increased by 47.9% year over year to US$112.2 million, and by 5.6% from US$106.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher traffic acquisition costs paid to third-party partners in relation to the expansion of BIGO Audience Network.

Shopline’s cost of revenues increased by 30.8% year over year to US$20.9 million, and by 13.9% from US$18.3 million in the second quarter of 2026. The year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter increases were primarily attributable to higher payment processing costs, reflecting an increased contribution from payment services to Shopline’s revenue mix.
